stops.note: the usual explanation is a Bantu word from the Kingdom of Kongo, whose contact with Portugal began when Diogo Cão reached the Congo River mouth in the 1480s
carried home by ships trading at Mpinda, Kongo's port on the river mouth; in Portuguese it still means any monkey
borrowed from Portuguese; much later, in 1799, the naturalist Lacépède made Macaca a scientific genus, narrowing it to mainly Asian monkeys
from French; the rhesus macaque later lent its name to the Rh blood factor, identified by Karl Landsteiner and Alexander Wiener in 1940
stops.meaning: Old World monkey of genus Macaca

current_meaning: an Old World monkey of the genus Macaca, such as the rhesus monkey
